title: Proliferation Transitions for Quantum Doubles of Groups
abstract: Proliferation transitions are phase transitions between a 2+1d topological order $\mathcal{T}$ and another $\mathcal{T}/\mathcal{A}$, obtained by condensing anyons in an algebra $\mathcal{A}\subset \mathcal{T}$. We consider such transitions in quantum doubles of groups, $\mathcal{T}=D(G, \omega)$, for finite groups $G$ possibly with three-cocycle $\omega$, for which condensable algebras are fully classified. Given a condensable algebra $\mathcal{A}$, we represent $\mathcal{T}$ in terms of a Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), that is tailored to the $\mathcal{A}$ proliferation transition. The SymTFT bulk is constructed from the Müger center of the subcategory generated by the algebra, i.e. the category of transparent lines, which can be bosons or fermions. Properties of the transition can then be inferred directly from the algebra classification data. For gauged Landau-Ginzburg (LG*) type transitions, we show that they do not only depend on the anyons in $\mathcal{A}$ through their field content, but the cubic interactions are fixed in terms of the multiplication structure of $\mathcal{A}$. Applied to twin algebras, which have the same anyon content but different multiplication structures, we show that twins result in distinct proliferation transitions.
subjects: Strongly Correlated Electrons (cond-mat.str-el) ; High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th); Quantum Algebra (math.QA)

title: Saturating $T^2$ resistivity in iron-based superconductors
abstract: Many correlated metals exhibit a crossover from low-temperature $\rho \propto T^{2}$ behavior to a slower increase of the resistivity at elevated temperatures. Distinguishing phonon scattering from electron--electron correlations as the origin of this crossover is experimentally challenging. We introduce a simple phenomenological framework that isolates the contribution responsible for the high-temperature saturating tendency. This approach reveals a clear contrast between systems well known for the predominance of electron--phonon scattering and several iron-based superconductors. For the latter, the conductivity can be expressed as the sum of a Fermi-liquid-like term ($\propto 1/T^{2}$) and a temperature-independent component, which together describe $\rho(T)$ up to $\sim 250$ K in LiFeAs, KFe$_2$As$_2$, and KCaFe$_4$As$_4$. In FeSe, the same approach identifies a similar regime above the nematic transition, with a pronounced change toward nearly linear-in-$T$ resistivity below it. We discuss these findings in the broader context of coherence and electronic correlations in Hund's metals.

title: Density Saturation and Autocorrelation Characteristics of Interlayer Exciton Ensembles in MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ Heterostructures
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 9 authors
abstract: We investigate interlayer excitons in MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterostructures using time-resolved photoluminescence and second-order autocorrelation measurements across a wide range of excitation powers and bath temperatures. By analyzing the photoluminescence amplitude and lifetime of the interlayer exciton state with the lowest emission energy, we extract a corresponding density-temperature diagram. The extracted exciton density exhibits a saturation at approximately $10^{13}$cm$^{-2}$, consistent with values predicted for a Mott transition of interlayer exciton ensembles in van der Waals heterostructures. Moreover, possible interpretations beyond the Mott transition are discussed. We further test whether the density limit is accompanied by a departure from classical photon statistics. The second-order autocorrelation measurements reveal that the photoluminescence maintains an emission characteristic of $g^{(2)}(0) \approx 1$ from low exciton densities up to the maximum reachable density in the investigated exciton ensembles consistent with the lowest-energy exciton ensemble obeying Poissonian statistics.

title: Field theories and critical excitations at anyon condensation transitions
abstract: Anyon condensation transitions remain challenging to characterize especially when the condensing anyons are non-abelian. We develop two complementary approaches for extracting information about the transition from the categorical data of the parent topological order and the condensate. The first adapts a Ginzburg-Landau procedure developed for $1+1$D transitions in the SymTFT setting to $2+1$D anyon condensation transitions. The construction applies when the anyons participating in the condensate have integer quantum dimensions. The second gives a criterion for identifying which point and loop excitations become critical at a continuous transition. The key step is to determine which anyon loops remain condensed throughout. All other loops become critical, while a point excitation becomes critical if it braids trivially with every condensed loop. We illustrate both proposals in several abelian and non-abelian examples.
subjects: Strongly Correlated Electrons (cond-mat.str-el) ; High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

title: Contrasting Crystal-Field and Dipolar Anisotropies in the Triangular Antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 13 authors
abstract: The magnetic ground states of rare-earth frustrated magnets can be governed by competing energy scales arising from crystal-field anisotropy, exchange interactions, and long-range dipolar interactions. Here we investigate this interplay in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$ by combining magnetization, specific heat, and neutron scattering measurements. Neutron powder diffraction resolves rotations of the ErO$_6$ octahedra and supports the lower-symmetry $R\bar{3}$ structure over the previously proposed $R\bar{3}m$ model. Magnetization measurements and inelastic neutron scattering establish an effective spin-1/2 description of its low-temperature magnetism with pronounced easy-axis anisotropy, arising from a well-isolated Kramers ground-state doublet separated from the first excited crystal-electric-field level by approximately 4 meV. Below $T_{\rm N}=0.1$ K, single-crystal neutron diffraction reveals A-type antiferromagnetic order with the ordered moment predominantly oriented within the $ab$ plane, despite the pronounced paramagnetic easy-axis anisotropy. The estimated dipolar interaction scale is comparable to $T_{\rm N}$, and classical dipolar-energy calculations for the observed stacking pattern favor an in-plane moment orientation. These results reveal contrasting crystal-field and dipolar anisotropies in determining the magnetic ground state of NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$.

title: Rare-earth tuning of magnetic entropy and interaction scales in K$_3$$Ln$(PO$_4$)$_2$ ($Ln$ = Yb, Gd) for adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 11 authors
abstract: Adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration (ADR) based on frustrated rare-earth magnets provides a promising route toward helium-free sub-Kelvin cooling, while balancing magnetic entropy and interaction scales is essential for optimizing the ADR functionalities. Here we investigate the low-temperature magnetic and ADR properties of the alkali rare-earth double phosphates K$_3$$Ln$(PO$_4$)$_2$ ($Ln$ = Yb, Gd), which crystallize in a monoclinic $P2_1/m$ structure containing distorted isosceles triangular lattices of rare-earth ions. Magnetization and specific heat measurements confirm the absence of long-range magnetic ordering down to 0.1 K in both compounds. Direct quasi-ADR measurements demonstrate strongly contrasting refrigeration behaviors: K$_3$Yb(PO$_4$)$_2$ reaches a minimum temperature of 29.8 mK from an initial state of 2 K and 6 T, whereas K$_3$Gd(PO$_4$)$_2$ exhibits extended hold times below 150 mK associated with its larger magnetic entropy reservoir. Crystal-electric-field calculations confirm a $J_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1/2$ ground-state doublet in K$_3$Yb(PO$_4$)$_2$, while thermodynamic analysis based on magnetic entropy and interaction scales accounts for the distinct ADR performance of the two compounds. These results identify K$_3$$Ln$(PO$_4$)$_2$ as a chemically robust platform for rare-earth-tunable solid-state ADR.

title: Generalized Spin Groups and Applications to Magnons
abstract: Spin groups provide the natural symmetry framework for the isotropic Heisenberg model, in which spin and lattice degrees of freedom are separable. They have recently found broad applications in describing electronic band structure, magnon band topology, and transport phenomena. However, a typical spin Hamiltonian describing magnons contains not only isotropic Heisenberg exchange but also anisotropic interactions induced by spin-orbit coupling (SOC), including the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction, the Gamma exchange, and the single-ion anisotropy (SIA), which strongly influence magnon properties. More recently, some studies have also revealed relativistic magnon transport phenomena in altermagnets. Such systems typically exhibit partial spin-lattice locking, but are commonly assumed to be described by conventional magnetic groups. Here, we develop a systematic symmetry framework, generalized spin groups, for magnons. We first classify the symmetries of Heisenberg, DM, Gamma, and SIA interactions. The resulting classification contains 6 spin-only groups, together with a total of 161 nontrivial spin groups. The symmetries of magnetically ordered phases are then obtained through spontaneous symmetry breaking of the corresponding parent groups for spin Hamiltonians. We also identify 6 spin-only groups for ordered states, which generate 90, 264, 157, 264, 387, and 598 nontrivial spin groups, respectively. Finally, we apply generalized spin groups to the magnon thermal conductivity and spin conductivity tensors and derive all the symmetry-allowed forms. Our results provide a unified symmetry framework for analyzing magnon transport both with and without SOC, yielding more refined constraints on magnon responses.

title: Thermodynamic Stability of Classical $\mathbb Z_2$ Lattice Gauge Models
abstract: Finite-temperature phases are traditionally studied through spontaneous symmetry breaking, but symmetry-breaking fields can remove their distinction, as in the Ising model. This motivates the search for stable nontrivial thermal phases without symmetry protection. For classical $\mathbb Z_2$ lattice gauge models with spins on $m$-dimensional cells in a fixed spatial dimension $d$, we prove joint analyticity of the thermodynamic free-energy density in temperature and perturbation strength at sufficiently low positive temperatures under sufficiently weak local perturbations, whenever $1\le m\le d-2$. Perturbations need not preserve internal or gauge symmetries and may include noncommuting quantum interactions. A separate high-temperature expansion yields an analytic region reaching infinite temperature at any fixed finite perturbation strength. These results establish thermodynamic stability and support the conjecture that low- and high-temperature regimes remain separated by a thermal transition without symmetry protection.
subjects: Statistical Mechanics (cond-mat.stat-mech) ; Other Condensed Matter (cond-mat.other); Strongly Correlated Electrons (cond-mat.str-el)

title: Programmable nonlinear rotation of acoustically levitated chiral stars
abstract: Acoustic levitation enables objects to be suspended and manipulated without physical contact, providing a versatile platform for studying the dynamics of freely suspended matter. Yet levitated objects, from droplets and thin films to particle assemblies, frequently rotate spontaneously, and this axial rotation often remains difficult to predict or control. There is no general understanding of how the shape of a levitated object determines whether it rotates, in which direction, or how its rotation changes with acoustic amplitude. Here, we establish how particle geometry and acoustic amplitude govern spontaneous rotation of acoustically levitated objects. We work with a family of shapes we call ``chiral stars'', within which we systematically vary handedness and number of arms. In a symmetric acoustic field, stars that preserve in-plane mirror symmetry do not rotate, while those that break it spontaneously rotate with a direction set by handedness. Beyond this symmetry requirement, we demonstrate that geometry, as encoded by the number of star arms, couples with acoustic amplitude to produce complex, nonlinear dynamics, including spontaneous reversal of rotation direction. To explain these behaviors, we develop a minimal torque model constrained by independent measurements of rotational drag, which captures the observed responses across all star geometries. We then demonstrate predictive power by designing a ``hybrid star'' with a prescribed amplitude-dependent response and reversal voltage. Our results not only establish how particle geometry and acoustic amplitude combine to govern rotation in acoustically levitated systems, but also reveal unanticipated higher-order couplings with the acoustic field. Beyond explaining spontaneous rotation, they open a route toward programmable rotational dynamics in acoustically levitated matter.

title: Moments of Random Permanents and Hafnians: A Replica Approach
abstract: Using contour-integral representations of the permanent and of the Hafnian, we turn the computation of their moments for random matrices into a replica calculation, analogous to that of the moments of the partition function of a mean-field spin glass. For the $2k$-th moment of $N\times N$ matrices with independent entries, the dominant saddle point is replica symmetric for $k>2$, and we obtain in closed form the exponential growth rate, the prefactor and the first $1/N$ correction, in agreement with exact enumerations. The growth rate depends only on whether the entries are real or complex; higher cumulants affect only the prefactor and the $1/N$ term. At $k=2$ the replica-symmetric solution becomes unstable, separating a power-law bulk of the distribution from a large-deviation tail, which we compute. The results apply to boson sampling with single photons and with squeezed light.
subjects: Disordered Systems and Neural Networks (cond-mat.dis-nn) ; Statistical Mechanics (cond-mat.stat-mech); Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

title: Classical-to-Quantum Transition in Blackbody Radiation Thermodynamics: Planck's Law without Statistical Assumptions
abstract: Inspired by Fermi's model of radiation-matter interaction, we investigate the classical dynamics of a closed, finite-energy system, in which matter is coupled to an electromagnetic field. We find that energy is progressively transferred to increasingly high-frequency field modes, so that the effective temperature of both matter and radiation approaches zero in the long-time limit - in sharp contradiction with the finite-temperature equilibrium assumed by classical blackbody thermodynamics. Requiring consistency with the Stefan-Boltzmann and Wien laws identifies a characteristic time $t_L$, at which both laws are simultaneously satisfied. Strikingly, classical spectra obtained for different energies and cavity sizes collapse onto the universal Planck distribution at $t_L$. We conjecture that quantum dynamical localization arrests the classical energy cascade at $t_L$, and that the Planck distribution emerges as a dynamical consequence of this arrest - without invoking any a priori statistical assumption.

title: Luther-Emery liquid in one-dimensional attractive Fermi gas
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 7 authors
abstract: One-dimensional (1D) interacting Fermi gases underpin a rich variety of quantum liquids, ranging from the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov paired state to the Luther-Emery liquid (LEL). Notably, the LEL-characterized by gapless excitations in charge or spin degree of freedom and gapped excitations in the other-has long been theoretically predicted but has eluded definitive experimental observation to date. By exactly solving the attractive Yang-Gaudin model via the Bethe ansatz, we fully determine the low-energy excitation spectra for both spin and charge channels. For fully paired fermions, the spectrum features gapped spin excitation coexisting with gapless charge excitation. We further employ bosonization to derive analytical expressions for the dynamical structure factor (DSF) of the gapped spin excitation, which is a long-standing challenge in this study. In the trapped gas, we find that the spin Bragg spectroscopy peak occurs at a much higher frequency than the charge-mode peak, where the splitting frequency between these two peaks scales approximately linearly with the interaction strength. Crucially, the spin gap manifests as a sharp threshold in the spin DSF, below which spectral weight is completely absent, proving a direct and unambiguous spectroscopic fingerprint of the LEL. Our work establishes quasi-1D trapped attractive Fermi gases as a pristine experimental platform for the long-sought direct observation of the LEL.

title: Emergent non-reciprocal pair interactions in catalytically propelled active polyhedra
abstract: Particle shape plays a fundamental role in the dynamics and pair interactions of active particles. Yet, experimental measurements of anisotropic active particles are largely lacking. Here, we introduce an experimental system that allows us to observe and measure the effective pair interactions of self-propelled active colloidal polyhedra. We realize such a system by 3D micro-printing quasi- 2D polyhedral colloids with edge number N= 3,4,5,6 and infinity and induce propulsion by partially coating them with an iridium catalytic cap and dispersing them in hydrazine. Despite their different geometries, all shapes exhibit similar single-particle positional dynamics. Stochastic Force Inference reveals predominantly radial, non-reciprocal pair interactions with similar attractive and repulsive regimes for all particle shapes at center-to center distances of about two particle diameters. A minimal plausible phoretic active-Brownian-particle model with a disc shape reproduces the experimentally observed behavior and identifies the physical origins: concentration-dependent slowing down sets their dominant angular symmetry, while the spatial geometry of the chemical coupling and phoretic attraction recover their relative magnitudes and angular dependence. We find that the shape anisotropy present in experiments only modulates the magnitudes and angular dependence of these interactions, and that these variations become more pronounced the stronger the anisotropy. Our results demonstrate the interplay of chemically mediated interactions and particle geometry-induced effects at intermediate interaction distances.

title: Collective Hall quantization in 3D Chern vector systems
abstract: Understanding the three-dimensional (3D) quantum Hall effect, characterized by a Chern vector rather than a single Chern number, has been a central pursuit in topological physics. While quantized Hall transport is established for the special case with one nonzero Chern component, recent realizations of more general Chern-vector states raise a fundamental question: how does such topology protect quantized transport? Here, we predict a distinct 3D quantized Hall effect protected by $\mathbf{C}=(0,m,n)$. For samples with dimensions $L_y$ and $L_z$, global topology enforces collective quantization of $mL_y+nL_z$, despite the fragility of individual edge modes to disorder. This reveals a novel transport regime in which robust quantization emerges as a holistic property of a unified chiral network,rather than of its constituent modes. Crucially, this collective response manifests as a quantized Hall conductance $G_{xy}=\pm(mL_y+nL_z)e^2/h$, with a distinctive dependence on both Chern-vector components and sample dimensions. We propose candidate materials to facilitate experimental observation.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)
comments: This manuscript substantially revises and supersedes our earlier preprint ( arXiv:2501.14493 ), with a restructured presentation and a different scientific emphasis

title: Suppression and reemergence of directional transport across the ferromagnetic transition in SrRuO$_3$
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 8 authors
abstract: SrRuO$_3$ is a canonical itinerant ferromagnet that continues to serve as a fertile platform for exploring spin-orbit coupled transport and topological responses in correlated oxide metals. Here, we investigate a (110)-oriented epitaxial SrRuO3 thin film on DyScO$_3$, where crystallographic anisotropy allows for symmetry-resolved charge transport along orthogonal in-plane directions. We uncover two principal findings. First, the resistance above the Curie temperature $T_{c,on}\approx 165$ K exhibits strong anisotropy, consistent with directionally dependent spin-fluctuation scattering. Below $T_{c,on}$, this anisotropy nearly vanishes, despite persistent structural inequivalence, due to isotropic electron-magnon and electron-electron scattering processes. Second, the application of a magnetic field reveals a striking directional contrast in the linear magnetoresistance (MR): it remains negative and saturates along [001], but changes sign and becomes positive along $[1\bar{1}0]$ below $T_0=145$ K. In contrast, the quadratic MR term is identical for both directions and peaks near $T_{\mathrm{OHE}}^*=155$ K, where the ordinary Hall coefficient crosses zero, consistent with carrier compensation under a two-band scenario. A sign change in the anomalous Hall signal at $T_{\mathrm{AHE}}^*=150$ K is consistent with a temperature-dependent redistribution of Berry-curvature contributions near the Fermi level. These results establish ferromagnetic ordering as the primary driver of the observed directional magnetotransport in SrRuO$_3$.

title: Andreev Scattering Driven Surface Photogalvanic Effect
abstract: The surface photogalvanic effect is a powerful tool for generating macroscopic direct currents in centrosymmetric film structures via asymmetric scattering of carriers at film boundaries. Here, we uncover a fundamentally distinct regime of photoinduced transport in normal metal-superconductor heterostructures, in which the macroscopic photocurrent is governed by Andreev scattering at the interface rather than by classical scattering. We demonstrate that the interplay between asymmetric surface scattering and Andreev retroreflection yields a giant, strongly frequency-dependent anomalous photocurrent. Strikingly, the electron-hole conversion at the normal-superconducting interface dictates a macroscopic sign reversal of the photogalvanic current across the superconducting transition, and induces non-analytic spectral kinks exactly at the pairing gap frequency. Our results establish the Andreev reflection-driven surface photogalvanic effect as a platform for optical control of superconducting correlations and suggest a direct, non-invasive spectroscopic probe for gap dynamics in hybrid quantum devices.

title: Pressure-induced superconductivity in a bilayer metal
abstract: We propose a model that explains the mechanism of pressure-induced superconductivity in a bilayer metal. Four types of pair potentials are assumed for a Cooper pair consisting of two electrons on different layers. Absence of local inversion symmetry gives rise to the spin-orbit coupling which is antisymmetric in the two layers. We assume that external pressure enhances the hybridization between the two layers. The stability of the superconducting states is well explained by the frequency symmetry of the induced pairing correlations by these potentials. Pressure-induced superconductivity emerges when the following two conditions are realized. (i) The spin-orbit coupling induces the odd-frequency pairing correlations and suppresses superconductivity at ambient pressure. (ii) The interplay between the spin-orbit coupling and the hybridization induces the additional pairing correlation that belongs to an even-frequency symmetry class. We briefly discuss the relevance of our model to real materials.

title: Lattice symmetry breaking and strain control of single-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetism in Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 10 authors
abstract: Distinguishing single-$\mathbf{q}$ from multi-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetism constrains microscopic spin Hamiltonians. Here we determine the ground state of the candidate Kitaev magnet Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$ through its coupling to the lattice. High-resolution neutron diffraction reveals a spontaneous monoclinic-to-triclinic distortion at the magnetic transition, in contrast to the absence of detectable lattice-symmetry breaking in triple-$\mathbf{q}$ Na$_2$Co$_2$TeO$_6$. Together with strain-selective magnetic responses, this identifies single-$\mathbf{q}$ order in Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$ over the proposed symmetry-preserving double-$\mathbf{q}$ state. Uniaxial compression along a low-symmetry in-plane direction achieves the domain selection that magnetic-field training could not, revealing the intrinsic field-induced phase boundaries of the dominant domain. These results establish strain as a symmetry-conjugate field for magnetic domains and highlight magnetoelastic coupling as a route to diagnose, manipulate, and potentially tune magnetic states.

title: Persistent Photo-Enhancement of Molecular Orbital Excitations in the Kondo Insulator FeSb$_2$
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 17 authors
abstract: When insulators are excited by photons with above-gap energies, photo-doped carriers are transiently generated. Typically, orbital excitations weaken and broaden due to increased screening by these transient carriers, followed by a few-ps recovery via phonon thermalization. Here we report the observation of anomalous dynamics of many-body molecular orbital excitations in the narrow-gap Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$. In the pumped X-ray absorption spectra following excitation with 1~$\mu$m photons, we observe a transient transfer of absorption intensity from the delocalized states at the main absorption peak to the localized molecular orbital states at the pre-edge. At the resonance of the low-energy molecular orbital excitations, the pumped resonant inelastic X-ray spectra show an approximately 30\% intensity increase at a pump fluence of 11 mJ/cm$^2$ concomitant with the emergence of an energy gain feature. While the energy gain feature disappears after about 1-2~ps, the increased molecular orbital excitation intensities partially persist for at least 50~ps with no discernible energy shift. These observations require the invocation of a many-body excitation picture beyond single particle population changes.

title: Magnetic-Field Effects on the Electronic States of the K$_4$ Lattice
abstract: We investigate the electronic states of the K$_4$ lattice in a uniform magnetic field within a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model. The K$_4$ lattice is a \rev{noncentrosymmetric three-dimensional network with triple-Dirac cones at the $\Gamma$ and H points}. By fixing the Bloch momentum component parallel to the field, the Peierls-substituted tight-binding problem reduces to an effective two-dimensional problem and yields a Hofstadter spectrum \rev{whose self-similar subpatterns reflect the geometry of the lattice projected onto the plane perpendicular to the field}. A square-like substructure emerges on the flux scale $\phi = 1/8$ for $\bm{B}\parallel[100]$, and honeycomb- and triangular-like substructures emerge on the finer scale $\phi = 1/32$ for $\bm{B}\parallel[111]$\rev{. Here $\phi$ is the flux through the elementary plaquette of the projected lattice, and these scales correspond to one flux quantum per projected unit cell. Owing to the screw axes of the chiral K$_4$ network, the field-parallel momentum acts as an additional flux, which, for commensurate values of this momentum, shifts the spectrum along the flux axis and brings the second triple-Dirac cone at the H point into the magnetic spectrum}. In the weak-field limit, we derive the Landau-level structure from a low-energy effective Hamiltonian around the $\Gamma$ point. The three-component nature of the triple-Dirac cone gives rise to a cubic secular equation, whose solutions describe how a pseudospin-flat branch coexists with two relativistic Landau ladders \rev{and a single chiral $n=0$ level dispersing linearly along the field, in agreement with the lattice calculation}.

title: Rashba-controlled emergence and reversal of critical-field anisotropy in p-wave magnet--superconductor hybrids
abstract: We show that tuning Rashba spin-orbit coupling can change the in-plane field direction along which an $s$-wave superconductor is most susceptible to Zeeman depairing. We consider a two-dimensional $s$-wave superconductor subject to an odd-parity exchange field induced by a $p$-wave magnet. Without Rashba coupling, the out-of-plane exchange field enhances the in-plane critical field but leaves its angular response exactly isotropic, despite the anisotropic magnetic spin texture. Minimizing the Bogoliubov--de Gennes grand potential over uniform singlet pairing, we find that increasing Rashba coupling first generates and then reverses the principal-axis critical-field contrast, switching the minimum-critical-field direction by $90^{\circ}$. Equal principal-axis fields at the intervening compensation point coexist with residual angular modulation. We interpret the reversal through competing momentum-dependent depairing contributions from the magnetic and Rashba spin textures, while the on-site singlet pairing channel remains unchanged. Direction-dependent discontinuous collapses of the order parameter further shape the critical-field curves. These results identify a tunable directional paramagnetic response within the uniform-pairing sector. In heterostructures with sufficient electrostatic tunability of interfacial Rashba coupling, this reversal would enable gate control of the easy-depairing axis without reorienting the magnetic texture.
comments: 14 pages, 10 figures. Submitted to Physical Review B on October 6, 2026

title: Charge-conserving creation and annihilation of topological phase singularities in atomically thin semiconductors
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 8 authors
abstract: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides provide a promising material platform for optical phase manipulation, as rapid variations in their dielectric functions can give rise to topological phase singularities (PSs). However, PS evolution while preserving topological charge conservation has not yet been investigated in exciton enabled PS systems. Here, using atomically thin MoS2 films on sapphire as a model system, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate that the evolution of dielectric dispersion determines the creation, trajectory, merging, and annihilation of optical PSs under topological charge conservation. By varying the MoS2 film thickness, we experimentally realize this evolution through the gradual shrinking of the high energy n-k dispersion loop, which modifies its intersection with the zero reflection condition. Our results provide a general strategy for exploring and manipulating topological optical states.

title: Magnetic-Field-Induced Darkening of Bright Excitons in a MoWSe$_2$ Monolayer Alloy
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 17 authors
abstract: Magnetic fields are widely used to brighten spin-forbidden dark excitons, but the inverse effect on an optically bright exciton has remained largely unexplored. We demonstrate the complementary phenomenon of magnetic-field-induced darkening of a bright exciton in Mo$_{0.68}$W$_{0.32}$Se$_2$. At 4.2 K, an in-plane magnetic field up to 25 T activates a dark-exciton line 14.2$\pm$1.3 meV below the bright exciton while suppressing the bright-exciton emission by about 85\%. A bright-dark mixing model quantitatively captures the coupled energy and intensity evolution with an effective in-plane $g$ factor of $|g_{\parallel}|=5.2\pm0.2$. Alloying is crucial to the effect, as it brings the system close to the bright-dark crossover, where a small bright-dark splitting is combined with unusually strong in-plane magnetic coupling. This places the system in a regime where field-induced level repulsion raises the bright-like branch and strongly depletes its thermal population. These results identify a general route to magnetic control of exciton populations through engineering of the bright-dark hierarchy.

title: Nanocrystalline cubic boron arsenide growth on GaAs(100) by gas source molecular beam epitaxy
abstract: Cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs) is a promising ultrahigh thermal conductivity semiconductor, but its direct synthesis on lattice-mismatched substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the synthesis of nanocrystalline c-BAs thin films on GaAs(100) substrates using gas source molecular beam epitaxy. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals an optimal growth temperature window of 250-400 C to maintain near stoichiometry and suppress severe arsenic loss. Surface and structural characterizations via atomic force microscopy, reflection high-energy electron diffraction, and grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction demonstrate a Volmer-Weber 3D island growth mode and a preferential crystallographic alignment with the GaAs substrate. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy confirms a chemically sharp interface without gallium interdiffusion into the c-BAs layer. These findings establish an initial step for the integration of c-BAs into advanced thermal and optoelectronic platforms.

title: Steering of topological criticality in the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain via non-Hermitian substitutional impurities
abstract: We investigate the topological phase in a one-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain in the presence of a finite concentration of non-Hermitian substitutional impurities. Our primary focus is the discovery of a deterministic mechanism to actively reconfigure the topological phase boundaries by introducing site-dependent, non-reciprocal intracell and intercell hopping amplitudes. Specifically, breaking the internal structural symmetry of the non-reciprocal impurity hoppings induces a targeted macroscopic displacement of the critical point. This mechanism allows for the controlled expansion or compression of the topological phase strictly via local defect asymmetry. We validate this boundary displacement through finite-size scaling analysis. The extracted correlation length critical exponents ($\nu \approx 1.455$ and $\nu \approx 1.397$ for symmetric and asymmetric configurations, respectively) confirm a disorder-induced departure from the pristine SSH universality class, with the exponent diverging at high defect densities. We also report an impurity-induced real-to-complex spectral transition geometrically characterized by the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect. Ultimately, our results establish how isolated non-Hermitian asymmetries cooperatively interact to deterministically shift macroscopic topological protection.

title: Chiral magnetic excitations in the RMn6Sn6 kagome metals (R=Tb, Ho, Er, and Y)
author_note: Showing the first 3 and last 3 of 12 authors
abstract: Recent inelastic neutron scattering (INS) investigations of the kagome metal TbMn6Sn6 reveal novel chiral magnetic excitations associated with the kagome layer. These excitations appear to have an itinerant character with a large energy scale (> 100 meV) and heavy damping; however, the origin of these excitations, which are not predicted by local moment linear spin-wave theory, is not understood. Here, we use INS to show that chiral excitations are also found in RMn6Sn6 compounds with R=Tb, Ho, Er, and Y having uniaxial, tilted, planar ferrimagnet, and planar double-spiral magnetic structures, respectively. Thus, the chiral excitations exist regardless of the magnetic structure. Additionally, R=Er and Y demonstrate that the chiral mode intensity is weaker in planar magnetic structures, suggesting that excitations are transverse to the local Mn moment direction. The chiral excitations appear only at L=odd positions in the Brilloun zone, and correspond to chiral spin exciations of the same handedness within each kagome layer, and pi out-of-phase between layers.

title: In Situ Thermal Preparation by CO$_2$-Laser and Chemical Characterization of Oxide Substrates Across Multiple Crystallographic Orientations
abstract: Atomically flat and chemically controlled oxide substrate surfaces are essential for high-quality epitaxial growth of complex materials and heterostructures. Previous studies have demonstrated in situ thermal preparation of selected oxide substrates, primarily focusing on conventional low-index orientations such as SrTiO$_3$ (100) and LaAlO$_3$ (100). Here, we extend these methodologies to a broader range of oxide substrates and crystallographic orientations, including challenging polar surfaces. We present a systematic study of the in situ thermal preparation of SrTiO$_3$ (100), SrTiO$_3$ (111), GdScO$_3$ (110), LaAlO$_3$ (111), (LaAlO$_3$)$_{0.3}$(Sr$_2$AlTaO$_6$)$_{0.7}$ (001), and NdGaO$_3$ (110) single crystal substrates. The substrates are annealed in a vacuum chamber under a controlled oxygen background environment using a CO$_2$ laser heating system. The optimized annealing conditions produce atomically flat step-and-terrace structures, long-range surface crystallinity, and effectively clean surfaces across all the investigated substrates. Our results establish a versatile, reproducible, and broadly applicable platform for the in situ preparation of oxide substrates immediately prior to epitaxial growth. These results also provide practical guidelines for interface engineering and surface-sensitive investigations of complex materials.

title: Structure and Dynamics of Defects in Two-Dimensional Nematic Liquid Crystals
abstract: Topological defects in nematic liquid crystals have recently received renewed interest due to their important role in non-equilibrium active materials and developing biological systems. While many studies have focused on simulating defect behaviors in these non-equilibrium situations, there has also been recent progress in our analytical understanding of defect morphology and behavior in a number of complicated regimes, such as intricate boundary conditions, anisotropic elasticity, or the presence of flows. Here, we review the analytical theory of disclination structure and dynamics in two-dimensional nematic liquid crystals, highlighting recent methods and results.

title: Density Accelerated Relaxation in Active Passive Colloidal Networks with Competing Interactions
abstract: We investigate quasi-2D active-passive colloidal mixtures with electric field-mediated non-identical interactions: unlike species attract and like species repel. Mapping the steady states across total area fraction and active particle area fraction identifies the regime of active percolated network formation among active fluid and clustered states. Within the percolated network regime, relaxation speeds up with increasing density, contrary to expectations for dense particulate gels. Particle-resolved dynamics and microstructure link this acceleration to activity-driven rearrangements enabled by asymmetric interactions.

title: Diffusive Description of Superconducting Single-Photon Detectors Using Quantum Mechanics
abstract: The methodology of non-Hermitian quantum mechanics is employed to parameterize the dynamics of coupled classical diffusion equations describing low- and high-energy quasiparticles in superconducting single-photon detectors in one to three spatial dimensions.

title: Ballistic transport and crystallographic control in altermagnetic quantum rings
abstract: We study coherent two-terminal transport through a finite-width $d$-wave altermagnetic quantum ring with nonmagnetic leads. A confined Aharonov--Bohm flux remains exactly $h/e$ periodic and, in the symmetric one-mode geometry, produces an exact half-flux transmission zero. A perpendicular field shifts the interference pattern according to an effective area $A_{\rm eff}=1.0342\,\pi r_0^2$ and the altermagnetic splitting resolves the common zero into nearby spin-dependent nodes. Rotating the crystal reverses the transmitted spin, whereas the mirror orientation $\theta_A=\pi/4$ is exactly spin degenerate. For a $50$~nm reference ring, sub-tesla fields yield windows with $|P_T|>0.99$, the most accessible of which requires a uniform field alone and no confined flux. Finite-bias, thermal, disorder, Zeeman, and spin-conserving voltage-probe calculations show that the polarization is appreciably more stable than individual coherent-resonance amplitudes. These results identify interference-node positions, flux periodicity, and crystal-controlled spin polarization as experimentally useful signatures of an altermagnetic mesoscopic interferometer.

title: Exact spectral integrability of a finite-channel random Schrödinger operator: from fermionization of the Dyson--Riccati gas to Kontsevich integral
abstract: We solve exactly, for arbitrary finite channel number $N$, the Riccati dynamics of a quasi-one-dimensional random matrix Schrödinger operator with Hermitian white-noise potential in the $\beta=2$ unitary symmetry class. The associated Dyson--Riccati eigenvalue gas admits an exact free-fermion representation at any sample length $L$, which in the limit $L\to \infty$ expresses the density of states and the total Lyapunov growth rate exactly through a single Airy Hankel $\tau$-function providing multichannel generalization of $N=1$ Halperin--Thouless formulas. The $\tau-$function further admits an outgoing-contour Kontsevich matrix Airy integral representation. Its saddle-point and double-scaling analyses give, in a unified way, the finite-channel density Lifshitz tail, and the large-$N$ spectral edge. In particular, for $N\gg 1$ the sharp $N=\infty$ edge is softened within an $N^{-4/5}$ spectral window, with its profile governed by the tritronquée solution of Painlevé I. We conjecture universality of this quasi-one-dimensional scaling edge profile for a broad class of $\beta=2$ random band matrices.

title: Quantum Oscillations across Hole Crystallization in Rhombohedral Graphene
abstract: Recent quantum-oscillation measurements in rhombohedral graphene reveal an abrupt increase in the dominant frequency and the emergence of additional frequencies as the carrier density is lowered toward superconductivity. Noninteracting band models can account for multiple frequencies but do not explain the upward jump. We show that these features can arise from two competing fates of the inner hole pocket in an annular Fermi sea: collapse into a simply connected Fermi liquid or crystallization into an anticrystal, in which localized holes coexist with itinerant electrons. Pocket collapse contracts the outer Fermi contour at fixed density, whereas hole crystallization preserves a larger contour that supports magnetic-breakdown orbits. This contrast provides a possible explanation for the frequency jump, while additional reconstructed orbits produce a multitone spectrum. Our results support the anticrystal as a candidate normal state near superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene.

title: Tailoring Dielectric Relaxation and Charge Transport in Amorphous Ge-Te-Se Phase-Change Materials through Yttrium Incorporation
abstract: The Te(1-x)(GeSe0.5)Yx (x = 0.05, 0.10, 0.15) alloys were prepared by a melt-quenching method and characterized using dielectric spectroscopy. The dielectric parameters and electrical conductivity were evaluated to assess their potential for phase-change memory and other electronic applications. The temperature and frequency dependence of the dielectric constants, ac conductivity, and dielectric loss of prepared chalcogenide glassy alloys were investigated over the frequency range 1 Hz - 1 MHz, and the temperature range 302 - 422 K, below the glass transition temperature. Both dielectric loss and dielectric constant were found to decrease with increasing frequency and decreasing temperature. The observed dielectric loss change was interpreted using the Guintini model of dielectric dispersion, correlated barrier hopping (CBH) model, and orientation polarization. The Cole-Cole analysis confirmed a distribution of relaxation times and yielded activation energies consistent with the CBH conduction mechanism. The frequency dependence of the ac conductivity follows the power law (A{\omega}s), where the frequency exponent (s < 1) decreases with increasing temperature, further supporting the CBH conduction mechanism. The incorporation of Y increases the density of localized tail states, resulting in enhanced ac conductivity. These findings suggest that the investigated materials are promising candidates for future phase-change memory and other electronic device applications.

title: Zeeman Quantum Geometry of the Layer Pseudo-spin
abstract: Two-dimensional layers coupled by position-dependent interlayer tunnelling host a layer pseudo-spin whose polarization is a controllable internal degree of freedom. We introduce the quantum geometry of this layer pseudo-spin: a mixed tensor formed from the interband Berry connection and the layer matrix element, which governs the response to an oscillating in-plane electric field. Because the layer pseudo-spin is an Ising-type scalar invariant under threefold rotation, its selection rules differ from those of a pseudovector spin. In a minimal two-band model, the layer-pseudo-spin quantum metric and Zeeman--Berry curvature are nonzero, while their zone integrals vanish. An in-plane drive therefore leaves the spatially averaged polarization unchanged at linear order but imprints a moiré-periodic intracell pattern, directly imageable by layer-resolved tunnelling. For twisted MoTe$_2$ bilayer, we quantify the local dipole modulation and identify the rectified, helicity-odd, and third-harmonic channels through which a net response appears at higher order.

title: Vortex matter as a magnetically programmable metasurface for tuning near-field radiative heat transfer
abstract: Near-field radiative heat transfer (NFRHT) is of great interest for energy conversion and thermal management. Recent work on NFRHT has shown that metasurfaces can enhance NFRHT and reshape its spectral characteristics. Here, we show that the vortex lattice of a type-II superconductor represents a self-assembled metasurface whose lattice dimensions, in contrast to most other metasurfaces, can be tuned by magnetic fields, allowing NFRHT to be varied by orders of magnitude. Specifically, we show that for two Nb surfaces at 4.2 K and separated by a 100 nm gap, NFRHT can be magnetically tuned by a factor >200. Further, we show that the tuning range grows upon cooling, exceeding 10^5 at 2 K, which is far beyond the order-unity modulation of many proposed schemes for tuning NFRHT. Our results establish vortex matter as a magnetically programmable thermal metasurface and open new opportunities for tuning the flow of heat at the nanoscale.

title: Emergent Active-Blob Length Scale Governs the Collapse Transition of Tangentially Driven Polymers
abstract: The coil-to-globule transition is a paradigmatic phenomenon in polymer physics and biophysics, in which polymer chains evolve from swollen to globular conformations upon decreasing solvent quality. At equilibrium, this transition can be rationalized in terms of a thermal blob length that diverges at the so-called $\Theta$ condition, marking the crossover from self-avoiding to globular conformations. How activity modifies this conformational transition and affects the fundamental length scales at play remains poorly understood. Here, we address this question for tangentially driven polymers using Brownian dynamics simulations, systematically varying both intrachain attraction strength and activity. We find that polar activity smears out the crossover from swollen to globular conformations. Between self-avoiding and $\Theta$ conditions, activity dominates by introducing an emergent folding length scale, which acts as an active blob length. In this regime, we demonstrate that the ratio of thermal to active length scales provides a new scaling variable that leads to a universal master curve for active polymer collapse.

title: Good-$Γ$ Numbers: A Shell-Optimized Route to the Thermodynamic Limit in Quantum Monte Carlo Calculations of the High-Density Two-Dimensional Electron Gas
abstract: Single-particle finite-size errors remain a central obstacle in quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations of periodic systems, conventionally reduced via twist averaging (TA). Here we introduce Good-$\Gamma$ (GG) particle numbers as system sizes $N$ at which the $\Gamma$-point Hartree--Fock (HF) energy of the high-density two-dimensional uniform electron gas (2D UEG) lies anomalously close to its thermodynamic-limit (TL) value. All results in this work concern the 2D UEG in its high-density Fermi-liquid regime, $r_s=1$--$4$. We systematically investigate the kinetic- and exchange-energy errors, $\Delta KE(N)$ and $\Delta EX(N)$, that underlie this one-body finite-size-error cancellation across four densities and both spin polarizations. We then compare diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) energies extrapolated to the TL from GG-$N$ sequences against twist-averaged extrapolations at the same densities and polarizations, finding agreement to within a fraction of a millihartree in every case, independent of whether a $1/N$ or an $N^{-5/4}$ extrapolation form is used.

title: Non-uniform grids to accelerate electron-phonon coupling calculations for superconductivity
abstract: Efficient and accurate evaluation of electron-phonon interactions is essential for predictive superconductivity calculations, but dense Brillouin zone sampling requirements pose a major computational bottleneck. To overcome this, we introduce an accelerated, highly scalable framework that combines a double delta truncation scheme with non-uniform Farey grids in both $\mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{q}$ space. The truncation strategy significantly reduces computational cost by restricting integration to states satisfying energy constraints near the Fermi level, while the Farey grids dynamically resolve sampling errors from localized scattering and stabilize convergence. Applied to elemental aluminium and several high-pressure hydrides, this combined methodology reduces computational cost by up to two orders of magnitude and yields electron-phonon coupling constants and superconducting critical temperatures Tc typically within about 5% of full-grid benchmarks. This approach overcomes sampling bottlenecks associated with dense uniform grids, making accurate, low-cost predictions of superconductivity in complex quantum materials feasible.
